title: An invertible module with trivial generic fibre over a flat family with integral fibres on a normal base is pulled back from the base

standard_prerequisites.name: A flat morphism with integral fibres over an integral base has integral source, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the trivializing section of the generic fibre into a regular meromorphic section on the source.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pullbacks of meromorphic functions along a morphism with integral fibres are defined, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the product of a pulled back meromorphic function with the chosen section to be considered.

standard_prerequisites.name: Structural facts about a normal local domain of dimension one: it is a discrete valuation ring, the intersection over height one primes with prescribed exponents equals a symbolic power expression, symbolic powers commute with flat base change and flat extensions intersect ideals, and a product of ideals equal to a principal ideal makes the factors finite locally free of rank one
standard_prerequisites.use: These are the algebra inputs of the affine computation that splits the section s into a product of a unit and an element coming from the base.

standard_prerequisites.name: The quotient topology statement for quasi-compact surjective flat morphisms and the openness statement for flat morphisms locally of finite presentation, cited from the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Decides the two cases of the hypothesis that the given morphism is either quasi-compact or locally of finite type, showing that the exceptional set is closed.

core_obligations: Set up the section: take the generic point of the target, note that the pullback of the invertible module to the generic fibre is trivial by hypothesis, choose a trivializing section, and use that the source is integral and that pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined to regard the section as a regular meromorphic section (proof lines 6983-6994).

Define the candidate module: consider the sheaf of meromorphic functions on the target whose product with the pulled back section lands in the invertible module on the source, and claim that it is invertible and that multiplication by the section is an isomorphism from its pullback to the given module (proof lines 6994-7002).

Prove the claim in the affine trivial case: write the section as a quotient of an element of the source ring by a nonzero element of the base ring, and equally as a quotient of a base element by a source element; using that the base is normal, control the symbolic powers of the finitely many minimal primes over the product of the two denominators, conclude that the corresponding ideals have product equal to the principal ideal generated by that product, apply the cited algebra lemma to see that they are finite locally free of rank one, and read off that locally the section is a unit times an element from the base (proof lines 7004-7043).

Globalize: at a point of the target, apply the affine result to the local rings, obtaining an element of the fraction field well defined up to a unit; for a second point over the same base point compare the two elements on a point of the intersection inside the fibre, which is nonempty because the fibre is irreducible, and conclude that the pulled back section generates the module on a neighbourhood of the whole fibre; the locus where it fails is closed and of the form the preimage of a subset not containing the base point (proof lines 7045-7064).

Finish: show that exceptional subset is closed. If the morphism is quasi-compact this is the cited quotient topology statement; if the morphism is locally of finite type it is open by the cited openness statement, so the complement of the exceptional subset is open as the image of the open complement of the bad locus (proof lines 7066-7090).
proof_roadmap: Choose a trivializing section on the generic fibre and build the candidate invertible module of meromorphic functions on the base (proof lines 6983-7002).

Settle the case of an affine trivial total space by a symbolic-power computation over a normal base (proof lines 7004-7043), then glue over the target using irreducibility of the fibres and the openness or quotient-topology hypothesis (proof lines 7045-7090).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a flat morphism with integral fibres from a locally Noetherian source onto a locally Noetherian integral normal base, an invertible module whose restriction to the generic fibre is trivial is the pullback of an invertible module on the base (statement lines 6967-6981). The counted proof is long and has three distinct layers: it produces a regular meromorphic section from a trivializing section of the generic fibre, defines the candidate module of meromorphic functions on the base and states the isomorphism claim, settles the affine case with a substantial symbolic-power computation over the normal base in which the product of the two ideals is shown to be principal so that both factors become invertible, and then glues over the target by comparing local generators along fibres, which is where the irreducibility of the fibres and the case hypothesis on the morphism are used to make the exceptional set closed (proof lines 6983-7090). It is H2: the argument is a complete author proof with real substance and the cited inputs are standard commutative algebra, but the author leaves 'some details omitted' in the glueing step, so no independent research-level claim is made.
